entry.title: BITCOS Layout Improves Ternary LLM Compression and Inference Efficiency
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | arxiv.org | hacker news

This distribution-adaptive layout optimizes the storage of ternary Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploiting high zero densities in weight distributions. While ternary models—using weights from $\{-1, 0, +1\}$—typically require approximately 1.585 bits per weight, the method uses a presence bitmap and a compacted sign vector to achieve a bit-width of $2 - z$ per weight, where $z$ is the zero density. This approach allows models to reach compression levels as low as 1.485 bits per weight, outperforming standard five-trit packing.

The layout is optimized for efficient unpacking on modern processors and GPUs, including AVX-512, AVX2, and Intel Xe2. Real-world tests show that the method can increase matrix-vector multiplication throughput by up to $1.28\times$. End-to-end inference testing across various platforms demonstrated decode throughput improvements of up to $1.18\times$ on CPUs and $1.27\times$ on GPUs.

Anthropic is merging its Claude chat and Cowork interfaces into a unified workspace, allowing users to access chat, Cowork, and Artifacts from a single window. The new design automatically routes requests to the appropriate tool, eliminating the need for users to manually switch between different tabs for different tasks.

The update also introduces new capabilities for creating, editing, and presenting documents and slides, with support for exporting files to PDF or PowerPoint. These features are rolling out first to Pro and Max subscribers across web, desktop, and mobile platforms, with plans to extend the rollout to free and team tiers in the coming weeks.
